disclaimer: Product controls mapped to Indian rules. Not legal advice and not a certification: applicability, durations and sufficiency are for qualified counsel, the privacy lead, a GST practitioner and the statutory auditor (Stage 47.16).

changelog.change: First India matrix (Stage 47.16.1): DPDP Act 2023, CERT-In directions 2022, IT Act s.43A, Companies Act and Accounts Rules, CGST Act and Rules, card payment data.

rows.rule: DPDP Act 2023 s.8(5): reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal-data breach
rows.trigger: Always - every client processes customer and staff personal data
rows.customer_duty: Grant roles on least privilege, keep MFA on for administrators, remove leavers
rows.control: Field-level read/write rules for personal, payroll, bank and secret fields; connector secrets encrypted at rest with a rotatable key; release suite fails on a committed secret or an unreviewed bypass
rows.retention: Not a record - a standing safeguard

rows.rule: DPDP Act 2023 s.8(6): notify the Data Protection Board and each affected person of a personal-data breach
rows.trigger: A personal-data breach is detected or reported
rows.customer_duty: Decide and send the notices for its own customers and staff; name who signs them
rows.control: Detection rules raise SECURITY_ALERT rows; a signed evidence pack for the incident window
rows.retention: Incident record and evidence pack kept off the ERP host for the life of the matter
rows.gap: No breach-notice workflow (who is affected, the notice text, the Board filing); Stage 49.12 and a legal decision on form and timing

rows.rule: DPDP Act 2023 s.8(7): erase personal data once its purpose is served or consent is withdrawn, unless a law requires it kept
rows.trigger: Consent withdrawn, account closed, or an erasure request
rows.customer_duty: Decide each request; set legal holds for disputes
rows.control: Approved erasure anonymises the customer and keeps the statutory sales and invoice rows; refused while a legal hold is set
rows.retention: Until the purpose ends; statutory financial records anonymised, not deleted
rows.gap: Customer subject only (Employee and Vendor requests refused); retention durations per category are [needs decision: 47.16.2]

rows.rule: DPDP Act 2023 ss.11-13: access, correction, erasure and grievance redress for the data principal
rows.customer_duty: Publish how to ask and who answers; answer within the time the Rules set
rows.control: Data-subject requests opened, decided by a different person (maker-checker), executed and evidenced
rows.retention: Request and decision kept as evidence
rows.gap: Customer subject only; no response-time clock on a request

rows.rule: DPDP Act 2023 s.6: consent for marketing, as easy to withdraw as to give
rows.customer_duty: Capture consent truthfully at the till and in forms
rows.control: Per-channel consent with its source and time on the customer; the send gate refuses a message without consent
rows.retention: Consent record kept while the customer record exists

rows.rule: DPDP Act 2023 ss.4-6: process personal data only for a lawful, stated purpose (data minimisation)
rows.trigger: Always - every personal field the product collects
rows.control: Field-purpose register: every personal or personal-looking doctype field has a purpose, basis, retention and readers; a new one without a row fails the build
rows.gap: Seven minimisation questions await the privacy owner; fields kept only in a document's JSON are outside the register

rows.rule: CERT-In directions 28 April 2022 (IT Act s.70B(6)): keep ICT system logs for a rolling 180 days within India
rows.trigger: Always - a body corporate operating ICT systems in India
rows.customer_duty: Host in India (or confirm the operator does); keep logs of its own devices and network
rows.control: The retention sweeps never delete a security-log row younger than 180 days, whatever the setting; audit trail never deleted
rows.gap: Host logs (web access log, journal, auth.log) can hold less than 180 days; residency of host and off-box backups is a per-deployment record

rows.rule: CERT-In directions 28 April 2022: synchronise ICT clocks to NIC or NPL NTP servers, or servers traceable to them
rows.trigger: Always - every server and device that writes logs
rows.customer_duty: Synchronise its own devices and on-premise servers
rows.control: None in the product; the host clock is the operating system's
rows.gap: No deploy step points the host at NIC/NPL time and nothing checks it is synchronised (proposed in cert-in-log-inventory.md section 3)

rows.rule: CERT-In directions 28 April 2022: report listed cyber incidents to CERT-In within six hours of noticing them
rows.customer_duty: Register a point of contact with CERT-In; file for incidents in its own business
rows.control: Detection rules, request tracing and a signed evidence pack; a six-hour workflow mapped to CERT-In's incident types
rows.retention: Incident record and pack for the life of the matter
rows.gap: Points of contact for the operator and each client are not registered; no drill has been timed against the six hours

rows.rule: IT Act 2000 s.43A and SPDI Rules 2011: reasonable security practices for sensitive personal data (passwords, financial information), until the DPDP Act's commencement omits s.43A
rows.trigger: The product holds passwords, bank and payroll data
rows.control: Passwords stored only as bcrypt hashes with a strength policy; bank and payroll fields readable by Super Admin only
rows.retention: Not a record - a standing safeguard

rows.rule: Companies (Accounts) Rules 2014 rule 3(1) proviso: accounting software keeps an audit trail of every change that cannot be disabled
rows.trigger: The client is a company keeping its books in the ERP
rows.control: Signed audit rows sealed into hourly checkpoints; a deleted or altered row is detected; audit writes can join the business transaction
rows.retention: Never deleted; sealed windows archived, encrypted and signed after at least 30 days
rows.gap: That every edit path writes an audit row with the before and after value is not proven for every document type

rows.rule: Companies Act 2013 s.128(5): keep books of account and vouchers for eight years
rows.customer_duty: Set the legal hold and retention it is advised to
rows.control: Posted financial documents are never swept; legal hold stops archiving and erasure
rows.retention: Eight years from the end of the financial year [needs decision: 47.16.4]
rows.gap: Retention durations per record class are not set; nothing yet proves an eight-year-old record is still restorable

rows.rule: Companies Act 2013 s.128 and CGST Act s.35: books stay as filed - no edit after a period is closed
rows.trigger: A period is closed for filing
rows.customer_duty: Close periods after filing; approve reopen requests only for a documented reason
rows.control: A closed accounting period refuses postings; reopening needs an approval

rows.rule: CGST Act 2017 s.36 and CGST Rule 56: keep accounts and records for 72 months from the annual return's due date
rows.customer_duty: Confirm the period with its GST practitioner
rows.control: Invoices, IRP attempts and events are evidence, never swept
rows.retention: 72 months from the due date of the annual return [needs decision: 47.16.4]
rows.gap: Retention is 'never swept', not a decided period with a legal-hold exit

rows.rule: CGST Rule 48(4): e-invoice (IRN) for B2B invoices above the notified turnover threshold
rows.trigger: Aggregate turnover above the notified threshold
rows.customer_duty: Register with an IRP or GSP and enter its credentials
rows.control: Invoices queued to the IRP with every attempt and event kept; the IRN and QR printed on the invoice
rows.gap: Live IRP/GSP credentials and certification stay with items 20.30/20.31/26.2.3/26.2.4

rows.rule: CGST Rule 138: e-way bill for goods moved above the notified value
rows.trigger: Goods moved above the notified consignment value
rows.customer_duty: Register on the e-way bill portal and enter its credentials
rows.control: E-way bill generated from the dispatch document; vehicle and transporter carried
rows.gap: Live portal credentials and certification stay with items 20.30/20.31/26.2.3/26.2.4

rows.rule: RBI card-data storage rules and PCI DSS: never store full card number, CVV, PIN or track data
rows.trigger: Card payments are taken at the till
rows.customer_duty: Use a certified terminal; confirm acquirer and PCI responsibilities in writing
rows.control: Only the provider's reference, terminal, amount and status are stored; the release suite fails on a card-data-shaped field
rows.retention: Payment references kept with the sale
rows.gap: Provider, acquirer and PCI responsibilities not yet confirmed (47.16.5)
